WHAT IF ONE THING CHANGES? (1)

FREQUENCY · VOLTAGE · LOAD · EXCITATION — THE RULES · TRANSFORMER

The rules (learn these 5 lines)

Excitation current I₀ = magnetising current Im (makes the flux, lags V by 90°) + core-loss current Iw (in phase). It is set by flux, not by load.

Flux rule: E = 4.44 f N φ → φ ∝ V/f. f ↑ at same V → φ ↓ → I₀ ↓. f ↓ at same V → φ ↑ → saturation → I₀ ↑↑. V/f constant → φ constant.

Losses: hysteresis Ph ∝ f·B1.6; eddy Pe ∝ f²B² ∝ V² (same V → eddy SAME). Copper loss ∝ I² (load). Reactance X = 2πfL ∝ f. 50 → 60 Hz at same V: φ × 0.83 · I₀ ↓ · Ph × 0.90 · Pe same · X × 1.2 · speed Ns × 1.2 · Tmax × 0.69.

Load ↑ changes currents and Cu loss only; flux and iron loss stay SAME (transformer, shunt motor). Excitation on a grid changes only Q (pf), never P or f.

Transformer

Excitation (no-load) current I₀ = magnetising current Im (makes flux) + core-loss current Iw. Core flux φm ∝ V/f (E = 4.44 f N φm).
